    86	BOOT_TIME = None  # set later
    87	# Used when reading "big" files, namely /proc/{pid}/smaps and /proc/net/*.
    88	# On Python 2, using a buffer with open() for such files may result in a
    89	# speedup, see: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/708
    90	BIGFILE_BUFFERING = -1 if PY3 else 8192
    91	LITTLE_ENDIAN = sys.byteorder == 'little'
    92	
    93	# "man iostat" states that sectors are equivalent with blocks and have
    94	# a size of 512 bytes. Despite this value can be queried at runtime
    95	# via /sys/block/{DISK}/queue/hw_sector_size and results may vary
    96	# between 1k, 2k, or 4k... 512 appears to be a magic constant used
    97	# throughout Linux source code:
    98	# * https://stackoverflow.com/a/38136179/376587
    99	# * https://lists.gt.net/linux/kernel/2241060
   100	# * https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1305
   101	# * https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/
   102	#     4f671fe2f9523a1ea206f63fe60a7c7b3a56d5c7/include/linux/bio.h#L99
   103	# * https://lkml.org/lkml/2015/8/17/234
   104	DISK_SECTOR_SIZE = 512

   209	def readlink(path):
   210	    """Wrapper around os.readlink()."""
   211	    assert isinstance(path, basestring), path
   212	    path = os.readlink(path)
   213	    # readlink() might return paths containing null bytes ('\x00')
   214	    # resulting in "TypeError: must be encoded string without NULL
   215	    # bytes, not str" errors when the string is passed to other
   216	    # fs-related functions (os.*, open(), ...).
   217	    # Apparently everything after '\x00' is garbage (we can have
   218	    # ' (deleted)', 'new' and possibly others), see:
   219	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/717
   220	    path = path.split('\x00')[0]
   221	    # Certain paths have ' (deleted)' appended. Usually this is
   222	    # bogus as the file actually exists. Even if it doesn't we
   223	    # don't care.
   224	    if path.endswith(' (deleted)') and not path_exists_strict(path):
   225	        path = path[:-10]
   226	    return path
   227	
   228	
   229	def file_flags_to_mode(flags):
   230	    """Convert file's open() flags into a readable string.
   231	    Used by Process.open_files().
   232	    """
   233	    modes_map = {os.O_RDONLY: 'r', os.O_WRONLY: 'w', os.O_RDWR: 'w+'}
   234	    mode = modes_map[flags & (os.O_RDONLY | os.O_WRONLY | os.O_RDWR)]
   235	    if flags & os.O_APPEND:
   236	        mode = mode.replace('w', 'a', 1)
   237	    mode = mode.replace('w+', 'r+')
   238	    # possible values: r, w, a, r+, a+
   239	    return mode
   240	
   241	
   242	def is_storage_device(name):
   243	    """Return True if the given name refers to a root device (e.g.
   244	    "sda", "nvme0n1") as opposed to a logical partition (e.g.  "sda1",
   245	    "nvme0n1p1"). If name is a virtual device (e.g. "loop1", "ram")
   246	    return True.
   247	    """
   248	    # Readapted from iostat source code, see:
   249	    # https://github.com/sysstat/sysstat/blob/
   250	    #     97912938cd476645b267280069e83b1c8dc0e1c7/common.c#L208
   251	    # Some devices may have a slash in their name (e.g. cciss/c0d0...).
   252	    name = name.replace('/', '!')
   253	    including_virtual = True
   254	    if including_virtual:
   255	        path = "/sys/block/%s" % name
   256	    else:
   257	        path = "/sys/block/%s/device" % name
   258	    return os.access(path, os.F_OK)
   259	
   260	
   261	@memoize
   262	def set_scputimes_ntuple(procfs_path):
   263	    """Set a namedtuple of variable fields depending on the CPU times
   264	    available on this Linux kernel version which may be:
   265	    (user, nice, system, idle, iowait, irq, softirq, [steal, [guest,
   266	     [guest_nice]]])
   267	    Used by cpu_times() function.
   268	    """
   269	    global scputimes
   270	    with open_binary('%s/stat' % procfs_path) as f:
   271	        values = f.readline().split()[1:]
   272	    fields = ['user', 'nice', 'system', 'idle', 'iowait', 'irq', 'softirq']
   273	    vlen = len(values)
   274	    if vlen >= 8:
   275	        # Linux >= 2.6.11
   276	        fields.append('steal')
   277	    if vlen >= 9:
   278	        # Linux >= 2.6.24
   279	        fields.append('guest')
   280	    if vlen >= 10:
   281	        # Linux >= 3.2.0
   282	        fields.append('guest_nice')
   283	    scputimes = namedtuple('scputimes', fields)
   284	
   285	
   286	def cat(fname, fallback=_DEFAULT, binary=True):
   287	    """Return file content.
   288	    fallback: the value returned in case the file does not exist or
   289	              cannot be read
   290	    binary: whether to open the file in binary or text mode.
   291	    """
   292	    try:
   293	        with open_binary(fname) if binary else open_text(fname) as f:
   294	            return f.read().strip()
   295	    except (IOError, OSError):
   296	        if fallback is not _DEFAULT:
   297	            return fallback
   298	        else:
   299	            raise
   300	
   301	
   302	try:
   303	    set_scputimes_ntuple("/proc")
   304	except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
   305	    # Don't want to crash at import time.
   306	    traceback.print_exc()
   307	    scputimes = namedtuple('scputimes', 'user system idle')(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

   310	# =====================================================================
   311	# --- prlimit
   312	# =====================================================================
   313	
   314	# Backport of resource.prlimit() for Python 2. Originally this was done
   315	# in C, but CentOS-6 which we use to create manylinux wheels is too old
   316	# and does not support prlimit() syscall. As such the resulting wheel
   317	# would not include prlimit(), even when installed on newer systems.
   318	# This is the only part of psutil using ctypes.
   319	
   320	prlimit = None
   321	try:
   322	    from resource import prlimit  # python >= 3.4
   323	except ImportError:
   324	    import ctypes
   325	
   326	    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
   327	
   328	    if hasattr(libc, "prlimit"):
   329	
   330	        def prlimit(pid, resource_, limits=None):
   331	            class StructRlimit(ctypes.Structure):
   332	                _fields_ = [('rlim_cur', ctypes.c_longlong),
   333	                            ('rlim_max', ctypes.c_longlong)]
   334	
   335	            current = StructRlimit()
   336	            if limits is None:
   337	                # get
   338	                ret = libc.prlimit(pid, resource_, None, ctypes.byref(current))
   339	            else:
   340	                # set
   341	                new = StructRlimit()
   342	                new.rlim_cur = limits[0]
   343	                new.rlim_max = limits[1]
   344	                ret = libc.prlimit(
   345	                    pid, resource_, ctypes.byref(new), ctypes.byref(current))
   346	
   347	            if ret != 0:
   348	                errno = ctypes.get_errno()
   349	                raise OSError(errno, os.strerror(errno))
   350	            return (current.rlim_cur, current.rlim_max)
   351	
   352	
   353	if prlimit is not None:
   354	    __extra__all__.extend(
   355	        [x for x in dir(cext) if x.startswith('RLIM') and x.isupper()])

   362	
   363	def calculate_avail_vmem(mems):
   364	    """Fallback for kernels < 3.14 where /proc/meminfo does not provide
   365	    "MemAvailable:" column, see:
   366	    https://blog.famzah.net/2014/09/24/
   367	    This code reimplements the algorithm outlined here:
   368	    https://git.kernel.org/cgit/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/
   369	        commit/?id=34e431b0ae398fc54ea69ff85ec700722c9da773
   370	
   371	    XXX: on recent kernels this calculation differs by ~1.5% than
   372	    "MemAvailable:" as it's calculated slightly differently, see:
   373	    https://gitlab.com/procps-ng/procps/issues/42
   374	    https://github.com/famzah/linux-memavailable-procfs/issues/2
   375	    It is still way more realistic than doing (free + cached) though.
   376	    """
   377	    # Fallback for very old distros. According to
   378	    # https://git.kernel.org/cgit/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/
   379	    #     commit/?id=34e431b0ae398fc54ea69ff85ec700722c9da773
   380	    # ...long ago "avail" was calculated as (free + cached).
   381	    # We might fallback in such cases:
   382	    # "Active(file)" not available: 2.6.28 / Dec 2008
   383	    # "Inactive(file)" not available: 2.6.28 / Dec 2008
   384	    # "SReclaimable:" not available: 2.6.19 / Nov 2006
   385	    # /proc/zoneinfo not available: 2.6.13 / Aug 2005
   386	    free = mems[b'MemFree:']
   387	    fallback = free + mems.get(b"Cached:", 0)
   388	    try:
   389	        lru_active_file = mems[b'Active(file):']
   390	        lru_inactive_file = mems[b'Inactive(file):']
   391	        slab_reclaimable = mems[b'SReclaimable:']
   392	    except KeyError:
   393	        return fallback
   394	    try:
   395	        f = open_binary('%s/zoneinfo' % get_procfs_path())
   396	    except IOError:
   397	        return fallback  # kernel 2.6.13
   398	
   399	    watermark_low = 0
   400	    with f:
   401	        for line in f:
   402	            line = line.strip()
   403	            if line.startswith(b'low'):
   404	                watermark_low += int(line.split()[1])
   405	    watermark_low *= PAGESIZE
   406	
   407	    avail = free - watermark_low
   408	    pagecache = lru_active_file + lru_inactive_file
   409	    pagecache -= min(pagecache / 2, watermark_low)
   410	    avail += pagecache
   411	    avail += slab_reclaimable - min(slab_reclaimable / 2.0, watermark_low)
   412	    return int(avail)
   413	
   414	
   415	def virtual_memory():
   416	    """Report virtual memory stats.
   417	    This implementation matches "free" and "vmstat -s" cmdline
   418	    utility values and procps-ng-3.3.12 source was used as a reference
   419	    (2016-09-18):
   420	    https://gitlab.com/procps-ng/procps/blob/
   421	        24fd2605c51fccc375ab0287cec33aa767f06718/proc/sysinfo.c
   422	    For reference, procps-ng-3.3.10 is the version available on Ubuntu
   423	    16.04.
   424	
   425	    Note about "available" memory: up until psutil 4.3 it was
   426	    calculated as "avail = (free + buffers + cached)". Now
   427	    "MemAvailable:" column (kernel 3.14) from /proc/meminfo is used as
   428	    it's more accurate.
   429	    That matches "available" column in newer versions of "free".
   430	    """
   431	    missing_fields = []
   432	    mems = {}
   433	    with open_binary('%s/meminfo' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   434	        for line in f:
   435	            fields = line.split()
   436	            mems[fields[0]] = int(fields[1]) * 1024
   437	
   438	    # /proc doc states that the available fields in /proc/meminfo vary
   439	    # by architecture and compile options, but these 3 values are also
   440	    # returned by sysinfo(2); as such we assume they are always there.
   441	    total = mems[b'MemTotal:']
   442	    free = mems[b'MemFree:']
   443	    try:
   444	        buffers = mems[b'Buffers:']
   445	    except KeyError:
   446	        # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1010
   447	        buffers = 0
   448	        missing_fields.append('buffers')
   449	    try:
   450	        cached = mems[b"Cached:"]
   451	    except KeyError:
   452	        cached = 0
   453	        missing_fields.append('cached')
   454	    else:
   455	        # "free" cmdline utility sums reclaimable to cached.
   456	        # Older versions of procps used to add slab memory instead.
   457	        # This got changed in:
   458	        # https://gitlab.com/procps-ng/procps/commit/
   459	        #     05d751c4f076a2f0118b914c5e51cfbb4762ad8e
   460	        cached += mems.get(b"SReclaimable:", 0)  # since kernel 2.6.19
   461	
   462	    try:
   463	        shared = mems[b'Shmem:']  # since kernel 2.6.32
   464	    except KeyError:
   465	        try:
   466	            shared = mems[b'MemShared:']  # kernels 2.4
   467	        except KeyError:
   468	            shared = 0
   469	            missing_fields.append('shared')
   470	
   471	    try:
   472	        active = mems[b"Active:"]
   473	    except KeyError:
   474	        active = 0
   475	        missing_fields.append('active')
   476	
   477	    try:
   478	        inactive = mems[b"Inactive:"]
   479	    except KeyError:
   480	        try:
   481	            inactive = \
   482	                mems[b"Inact_dirty:"] + \
   483	                mems[b"Inact_clean:"] + \
   484	                mems[b"Inact_laundry:"]
   485	        except KeyError:
   486	            inactive = 0
   487	            missing_fields.append('inactive')
   488	
   489	    try:
   490	        slab = mems[b"Slab:"]
   491	    except KeyError:
   492	        slab = 0
   493	
   494	    used = total - free - cached - buffers
   495	    if used < 0:
   496	        # May be symptomatic of running within a LCX container where such
   497	        # values will be dramatically distorted over those of the host.
   498	        used = total - free
   499	
   500	    # - starting from 4.4.0 we match free's "available" column.
   501	    #   Before 4.4.0 we calculated it as (free + buffers + cached)
   502	    #   which matched htop.
   503	    # - free and htop available memory differs as per:
   504	    #   http://askubuntu.com/a/369589
   505	    #   http://unix.stackexchange.com/a/65852/168884
   506	    # - MemAvailable has been introduced in kernel 3.14
   507	    try:
   508	        avail = mems[b'MemAvailable:']
   509	    except KeyError:
   510	        avail = calculate_avail_vmem(mems)
   511	
   512	    if avail < 0:
   513	        avail = 0
   514	        missing_fields.append('available')
   515	
   516	    # If avail is greater than total or our calculation overflows,
   517	    # that's symptomatic of running within a LCX container where such
   518	    # values will be dramatically distorted over those of the host.
   519	    # https://gitlab.com/procps-ng/procps/blob/
   520	    #     24fd2605c51fccc375ab0287cec33aa767f06718/proc/sysinfo.c#L764
   521	    if avail > total:
   522	        avail = free
   523	
   524	    percent = usage_percent((total - avail), total, round_=1)
   525	
   526	    # Warn about missing metrics which are set to 0.
   527	    if missing_fields:
   528	        msg = "%s memory stats couldn't be determined and %s set to 0" % (
   529	            ", ".join(missing_fields),
   530	            "was" if len(missing_fields) == 1 else "were")
   531	        warnings.warn(msg, RuntimeWarning)
   532	
   533	    return svmem(total, avail, percent, used, free,
   534	                 active, inactive, buffers, cached, shared, slab)
   535	
   536	
   537	def swap_memory():
   538	    """Return swap memory metrics."""
   539	    mems = {}
   540	    with open_binary('%s/meminfo' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   541	        for line in f:
   542	            fields = line.split()
   543	            mems[fields[0]] = int(fields[1]) * 1024
   544	    # We prefer /proc/meminfo over sysinfo() syscall so that
   545	    # psutil.PROCFS_PATH can be used in order to allow retrieval
   546	    # for linux containers, see:
   547	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1015
   548	    try:
   549	        total = mems[b'SwapTotal:']
   550	        free = mems[b'SwapFree:']
   551	    except KeyError:
   552	        _, _, _, _, total, free, unit_multiplier = cext.linux_sysinfo()
   553	        total *= unit_multiplier
   554	        free *= unit_multiplier
   555	
   556	    used = total - free
   557	    percent = usage_percent(used, total, round_=1)
   558	    # get pgin/pgouts
   559	    try:
   560	        f = open_binary("%s/vmstat" % get_procfs_path())
   561	    except IOError as err:
   562	        # see https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/722
   563	        msg = "'sin' and 'sout' swap memory stats couldn't " \
   564	              "be determined and were set to 0 (%s)" % str(err)
   565	        warnings.warn(msg, RuntimeWarning)
   566	        sin = sout = 0
   567	    else:
   568	        with f:
   569	            sin = sout = None
   570	            for line in f:
   571	                # values are expressed in 4 kilo bytes, we want
   572	                # bytes instead
   573	                if line.startswith(b'pswpin'):
   574	                    sin = int(line.split(b' ')[1]) * 4 * 1024
   575	                elif line.startswith(b'pswpout'):
   576	                    sout = int(line.split(b' ')[1]) * 4 * 1024
   577	                if sin is not None and sout is not None:
   578	                    break
   579	            else:
   580	                # we might get here when dealing with exotic Linux
   581	                # flavors, see:
   582	                # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/313
   583	                msg = "'sin' and 'sout' swap memory stats couldn't " \
   584	                      "be determined and were set to 0"
   585	                warnings.warn(msg, RuntimeWarning)
   586	                sin = sout = 0
   587	    return _common.sswap(total, used, free, percent, sin, sout)
   588	
   589	
   590	# =====================================================================
   591	# --- CPU
   592	# =====================================================================
   593	
   594	
   595	def cpu_times():
   596	    """Return a named tuple representing the following system-wide
   597	    CPU times:
   598	    (user, nice, system, idle, iowait, irq, softirq [steal, [guest,
   599	     [guest_nice]]])
   600	    Last 3 fields may not be available on all Linux kernel versions.
   601	    """
   602	    procfs_path = get_procfs_path()
   603	    set_scputimes_ntuple(procfs_path)
   604	    with open_binary('%s/stat' % procfs_path) as f:
   605	        values = f.readline().split()
   606	    fields = values[1:len(scputimes._fields) + 1]
   607	    fields = [float(x) / CLOCK_TICKS for x in fields]
   608	    return scputimes(*fields)
   609	
   610	
   611	def per_cpu_times():
   612	    """Return a list of namedtuple representing the CPU times
   613	    for every CPU available on the system.
   614	    """
   615	    procfs_path = get_procfs_path()
   616	    set_scputimes_ntuple(procfs_path)
   617	    cpus = []
   618	    with open_binary('%s/stat' % procfs_path) as f:
   619	        # get rid of the first line which refers to system wide CPU stats
   620	        f.readline()
   621	        for line in f:
   622	            if line.startswith(b'cpu'):
   623	                values = line.split()
   624	                fields = values[1:len(scputimes._fields) + 1]
   625	                fields = [float(x) / CLOCK_TICKS for x in fields]
   626	                entry = scputimes(*fields)
   627	                cpus.append(entry)
   628	        return cpus
   629	
   630	
   631	def cpu_count_logical():
   632	    """Return the number of logical CPUs in the system."""
   633	    try:
   634	        return os.sysconf("SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN")
   635	    except ValueError:
   636	        # as a second fallback we try to parse /proc/cpuinfo
   637	        num = 0
   638	        with open_binary('%s/cpuinfo' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   639	            for line in f:
   640	                if line.lower().startswith(b'processor'):
   641	                    num += 1
   642	
   643	        # unknown format (e.g. amrel/sparc architectures), see:
   644	        # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/200
   645	        # try to parse /proc/stat as a last resort
   646	        if num == 0:
   647	            search = re.compile(r'cpu\d')
   648	            with open_text('%s/stat' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   649	                for line in f:
   650	                    line = line.split(' ')[0]
   651	                    if search.match(line):
   652	                        num += 1
   653	
   654	        if num == 0:
   655	            # mimic os.cpu_count()
   656	            return None
   657	        return num
   658	
   659	
   660	def cpu_count_cores():
   661	    """Return the number of CPU cores in the system."""
   662	    # Method #1
   663	    ls = set()
   664	    # These 2 files are the same but */core_cpus_list is newer while
   665	    # */thread_siblings_list is deprecated and may disappear in the future.
   666	    # https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/admin-guide/cputopology.rst
   667	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/pull/1727#issuecomment-707624964
   668	    # https://lkml.org/lkml/2019/2/26/41
   669	    p1 = "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[0-9]*/topology/core_cpus_list"
   670	    p2 = "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[0-9]*/topology/thread_siblings_list"
   671	    for path in glob.glob(p1) or glob.glob(p2):
   672	        with open_binary(path) as f:
   673	            ls.add(f.read().strip())
   674	    result = len(ls)
   675	    if result != 0:
   676	        return result
   677	
   678	    # Method #2
   679	    mapping = {}
   680	    current_info = {}
   681	    with open_binary('%s/cpuinfo' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   682	        for line in f:
   683	            line = line.strip().lower()
   684	            if not line:
   685	                # new section
   686	                try:
   687	                    mapping[current_info[b'physical id']] = \
   688	                        current_info[b'cpu cores']
   689	                except KeyError:
   690	                    pass
   691	                current_info = {}
   692	            else:
   693	                # ongoing section
   694	                if line.startswith((b'physical id', b'cpu cores')):
   695	                    key, value = line.split(b'\t:', 1)
   696	                    current_info[key] = int(value)
   697	
   698	    result = sum(mapping.values())
   699	    return result or None  # mimic os.cpu_count()
   700	
   701	
   702	def cpu_stats():
   703	    """Return various CPU stats as a named tuple."""
   704	    with open_binary('%s/stat' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   705	        ctx_switches = None
   706	        interrupts = None
   707	        soft_interrupts = None
   708	        for line in f:
   709	            if line.startswith(b'ctxt'):
   710	                ctx_switches = int(line.split()[1])
   711	            elif line.startswith(b'intr'):
   712	                interrupts = int(line.split()[1])
   713	            elif line.startswith(b'softirq'):
   714	                soft_interrupts = int(line.split()[1])
   715	            if ctx_switches is not None and soft_interrupts is not None \
   716	                    and interrupts is not None:
   717	                break
   718	    syscalls = 0
   719	    return _common.scpustats(
   720	        ctx_switches, interrupts, soft_interrupts, syscalls)
   721	
   722	
   723	def _cpu_get_cpuinfo_freq():
   724	    """Return current CPU frequency from cpuinfo if available.
   725	    """
   726	    ret = []
   727	    with open_binary('%s/cpuinfo' % get_procfs_path()) as f:
   728	        for line in f:
   729	            if line.lower().startswith(b'cpu mhz'):
   730	                ret.append(float(line.split(b':', 1)[1]))
   731	    return ret
   732	
   733	
   734	if os.path.exists("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy0") or \
   735	        os.path.exists("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq"):
   736	    def cpu_freq():
   737	        """Return frequency metrics for all CPUs.
   738	        Contrarily to other OSes, Linux updates these values in
   739	        real-time.
   740	        """
   741	        cpuinfo_freqs = _cpu_get_cpuinfo_freq()
   742	        paths = \
   743	            glob.glob("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy[0-9]*") or \
   744	            glob.glob("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu[0-9]*/cpufreq")
   745	        paths.sort(key=lambda x: int(re.search(r"[0-9]+", x).group()))
   746	        ret = []
   747	        pjoin = os.path.join
   748	        for i, path in enumerate(paths):
   749	            if len(paths) == len(cpuinfo_freqs):
   750	                # take cached value from cpuinfo if available, see:
   751	                # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1851
   752	                curr = cpuinfo_freqs[i]
   753	            else:
   754	                curr = cat(pjoin(path, "scaling_cur_freq"), fallback=None)
   755	            if curr is None:
   756	                # Likely an old RedHat, see:
   757	                # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1071
   758	                curr = cat(pjoin(path, "cpuinfo_cur_freq"), fallback=None)
   759	                if curr is None:
   760	                    raise NotImplementedError(
   761	                        "can't find current frequency file")
   762	            curr = int(curr) / 1000
   763	            max_ = int(cat(pjoin(path, "scaling_max_freq"))) / 1000
   764	            min_ = int(cat(pjoin(path, "scaling_min_freq"))) / 1000
   765	            ret.append(_common.scpufreq(curr, min_, max_))
   766	        return ret
   767	
   768	else:
   769	    def cpu_freq():
   770	        """Alternate implementation using /proc/cpuinfo.
   771	        min and max frequencies are not available and are set to None.
   772	        """
   773	        return [_common.scpufreq(x, 0., 0.) for x in _cpu_get_cpuinfo_freq()]
   774
