   780	
   781	net_if_addrs = cext_posix.net_if_addrs
   782	
   783	
   784	class _Ipv6UnsupportedError(Exception):
   785	    pass
   786	
   787	
   788	class Connections:
   789	    """A wrapper on top of /proc/net/* files, retrieving per-process
   790	    and system-wide open connections (TCP, UDP, UNIX) similarly to
   791	    "netstat -an".
   792	
   793	    Note: in case of UNIX sockets we're only able to determine the
   794	    local endpoint/path, not the one it's connected to.
   795	    According to [1] it would be possible but not easily.
   796	
   797	    [1] http://serverfault.com/a/417946
   798	    """
   799	
   800	    def __init__(self):
   801	        # The string represents the basename of the corresponding
   802	        # /proc/net/{proto_name} file.
   803	        tcp4 = ("tcp", socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
   804	        tcp6 = ("tcp6", socket.AF_INET6, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
   805	        udp4 = ("udp", socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
   806	        udp6 = ("udp6", socket.AF_INET6, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
   807	        unix = ("unix", socket.AF_UNIX, None)
   808	        self.tmap = {
   809	            "all": (tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6, unix),
   810	            "tcp": (tcp4, tcp6),
   811	            "tcp4": (tcp4,),
   812	            "tcp6": (tcp6,),
   813	            "udp": (udp4, udp6),
   814	            "udp4": (udp4,),
   815	            "udp6": (udp6,),
   816	            "unix": (unix,),
   817	            "inet": (tcp4, tcp6, udp4, udp6),
   818	            "inet4": (tcp4, udp4),
   819	            "inet6": (tcp6, udp6),
   820	        }
   821	        self._procfs_path = None
   822	
   823	    def get_proc_inodes(self, pid):
   824	        inodes = defaultdict(list)
   825	        for fd in os.listdir("%s/%s/fd" % (self._procfs_path, pid)):
   826	            try:
   827	                inode = readlink("%s/%s/fd/%s" % (self._procfs_path, pid, fd))
   828	            except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
   829	                # ENOENT == file which is gone in the meantime;
   830	                # os.stat('/proc/%s' % self.pid) will be done later
   831	                # to force NSP (if it's the case)
   832	                continue
   833	            except OSError as err:
   834	                if err.errno == errno.EINVAL:
   835	                    # not a link
   836	                    continue
   837	                if err.errno == errno.ENAMETOOLONG:
   838	                    # file name too long
   839	                    debug(err)
   840	                    continue
   841	                raise
   842	            else:
   843	                if inode.startswith('socket:['):
   844	                    # the process is using a socket
   845	                    inode = inode[8:][:-1]
   846	                    inodes[inode].append((pid, int(fd)))
   847	        return inodes
   848	
   849	    def get_all_inodes(self):
   850	        inodes = {}
   851	        for pid in pids():
   852	            try:
   853	                inodes.update(self.get_proc_inodes(pid))
   854	            except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
   855	                # os.listdir() is gonna raise a lot of access denied
   856	                # exceptions in case of unprivileged user; that's fine
   857	                # as we'll just end up returning a connection with PID
   858	                # and fd set to None anyway.
   859	                # Both netstat -an and lsof does the same so it's
   860	                # unlikely we can do any better.
   861	                # ENOENT just means a PID disappeared on us.
   862	                continue
   863	        return inodes
   864	
   865	    @staticmethod
   866	    def decode_address(addr, family):
   867	        """Accept an "ip:port" address as displayed in /proc/net/*
   868	        and convert it into a human readable form, like:
   869	
   870	        "0500000A:0016" -> ("10.0.0.5", 22)
   871	        "0000000000000000FFFF00000100007F:9E49" -> ("::ffff:127.0.0.1", 40521)
   872	
   873	        The IP address portion is a little or big endian four-byte
   874	        hexadecimal number; that is, the least significant byte is listed
   875	        first, so we need to reverse the order of the bytes to convert it
   876	        to an IP address.
   877	        The port is represented as a two-byte hexadecimal number.
   878	
   879	        Reference:
   880	        http://linuxdevcenter.com/pub/a/linux/2000/11/16/LinuxAdmin.html
   881	        """
   882	        ip, port = addr.split(':')
   883	        port = int(port, 16)
   884	        # this usually refers to a local socket in listen mode with
   885	        # no end-points connected
   886	        if not port:
   887	            return ()
   888	        if PY3:
   889	            ip = ip.encode('ascii')
   890	        if family == socket.AF_INET:
   891	            # see: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/201
   892	            if LITTLE_ENDIAN:
   893	                ip = socket.inet_ntop(family, base64.b16decode(ip)[::-1])
   894	            else:
   895	                ip = socket.inet_ntop(family, base64.b16decode(ip))
   896	        else:  # IPv6
   897	            ip = base64.b16decode(ip)
   898	            try:
   899	                # see: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/201
   900	                if LITTLE_ENDIAN:
   901	                    ip = socket.inet_ntop(
   902	                        socket.AF_INET6,
   903	                        struct.pack('>4I', *struct.unpack('<4I', ip)))
   904	                else:
   905	                    ip = socket.inet_ntop(
   906	                        socket.AF_INET6,
   907	                        struct.pack('<4I', *struct.unpack('<4I', ip)))
   908	            except ValueError:
   909	                # see: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/623
   910	                if not supports_ipv6():
   911	                    raise _Ipv6UnsupportedError
   912	                else:
   913	                    raise
   914	        return _common.addr(ip, port)
   915	
   916	    @staticmethod
   917	    def process_inet(file, family, type_, inodes, filter_pid=None):
   918	        """Parse /proc/net/tcp* and /proc/net/udp* files."""
   919	        if file.endswith('6') and not os.path.exists(file):
   920	            # IPv6 not supported
   921	            return
   922	        with open_text(file, buffering=BIGFILE_BUFFERING) as f:
   923	            f.readline()  # skip the first line
   924	            for lineno, line in enumerate(f, 1):
   925	                try:
   926	                    _, laddr, raddr, status, _, _, _, _, _, inode = \
   927	                        line.split()[:10]
   928	                except ValueError:
   929	                    raise RuntimeError(
   930	                        "error while parsing %s; malformed line %s %r" % (
   931	                            file, lineno, line))
   932	                if inode in inodes:
   933	                    # # We assume inet sockets are unique, so we error
   934	                    # # out if there are multiple references to the
   935	                    # # same inode. We won't do this for UNIX sockets.
   936	                    # if len(inodes[inode]) > 1 and family != socket.AF_UNIX:
   937	                    #     raise ValueError("ambiguos inode with multiple "
   938	                    #                      "PIDs references")
   939	                    pid, fd = inodes[inode][0]
   940	                else:
   941	                    pid, fd = None, -1
   942	                if filter_pid is not None and filter_pid != pid:
   943	                    continue
   944	                else:
   945	                    if type_ == socket.SOCK_STREAM:
   946	                        status = TCP_STATUSES[status]
   947	                    else:
   948	                        status = _common.CONN_NONE
   949	                    try:
   950	                        laddr = Connections.decode_address(laddr, family)
   951	                        raddr = Connections.decode_address(raddr, family)
   952	                    except _Ipv6UnsupportedError:
   953	                        continue
   954	                    yield (fd, family, type_, laddr, raddr, status, pid)
   955	
   956	    @staticmethod
   957	    def process_unix(file, family, inodes, filter_pid=None):
   958	        """Parse /proc/net/unix files."""
   959	        with open_text(file, buffering=BIGFILE_BUFFERING) as f:
   960	            f.readline()  # skip the first line
   961	            for line in f:
   962	                tokens = line.split()
   963	                try:
   964	                    _, _, _, _, type_, _, inode = tokens[0:7]
   965	                except ValueError:
   966	                    if ' ' not in line:
   967	                        # see: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/766
   968	                        continue
   969	                    raise RuntimeError(
   970	                        "error while parsing %s; malformed line %r" % (
   971	                            file, line))
   972	                if inode in inodes:
   973	                    # With UNIX sockets we can have a single inode
   974	                    # referencing many file descriptors.
   975	                    pairs = inodes[inode]
   976	                else:
   977	                    pairs = [(None, -1)]
   978	                for pid, fd in pairs:
   979	                    if filter_pid is not None and filter_pid != pid:
   980	                        continue
   981	                    else:
   982	                        if len(tokens) == 8:
   983	                            path = tokens[-1]
   984	                        else:
   985	                            path = ""
   986	                        type_ = _common.socktype_to_enum(int(type_))
   987	                        # XXX: determining the remote endpoint of a
   988	                        # UNIX socket on Linux is not possible, see:
   989	                        # https://serverfault.com/questions/252723/
   990	                        raddr = ""
   991	                        status = _common.CONN_NONE
   992	                        yield (fd, family, type_, path, raddr, status, pid)
   993	
   994	    def retrieve(self, kind, pid=None):
   995	        if kind not in self.tmap:
   996	            raise ValueError("invalid %r kind argument; choose between %s"
   997	                             % (kind, ', '.join([repr(x) for x in self.tmap])))
   998	        self._procfs_path = get_procfs_path()
   999	        if pid is not None:
  1000	            inodes = self.get_proc_inodes(pid)
  1001	            if not inodes:
  1002	                # no connections for this process
  1003	                return []
  1004	        else:
  1005	            inodes = self.get_all_inodes()
  1006	        ret = set()
  1007	        for proto_name, family, type_ in self.tmap[kind]:
  1008	            path = "%s/net/%s" % (self._procfs_path, proto_name)
  1009	            if family in (socket.AF_INET, socket.AF_INET6):
  1010	                ls = self.process_inet(
  1011	                    path, family, type_, inodes, filter_pid=pid)
  1012	            else:
  1013	                ls = self.process_unix(
  1014	                    path, family, inodes, filter_pid=pid)
  1015	            for fd, family, type_, laddr, raddr, status, bound_pid in ls:
  1016	                if pid:
  1017	                    conn = _common.pconn(fd, family, type_, laddr, raddr,
  1018	                                         status)
  1019	                else:
  1020	                    conn = _common.sconn(fd, family, type_, laddr, raddr,
  1021	                                         status, bound_pid)
  1022	                ret.add(conn)
  1023	        return list(ret)
  1024	
  1025	
  1026	_connections = Connections()
  1027	
  1028	
  1029	def net_connections(kind='inet'):
  1030	    """Return system-wide open connections."""
  1031	    return _connections.retrieve(kind)
  1032	
  1033	
  1034	def net_io_counters():
  1035	    """Return network I/O statistics for every network interface
  1036	    installed on the system as a dict of raw tuples.
  1037	    """
  1038	    with open_text("%s/net/dev" % get_procfs_path()) as f:
  1039	        lines = f.readlines()
  1040	    retdict = {}
  1041	    for line in lines[2:]:
  1042	        colon = line.rfind(':')
  1043	        assert colon > 0, repr(line)
  1044	        name = line[:colon].strip()
  1045	        fields = line[colon + 1:].strip().split()
  1046	
  1047	        # in
  1048	        (bytes_recv,
  1049	         packets_recv,
  1050	         errin,
  1051	         dropin,
  1052	         fifoin,  # unused
  1053	         framein,  # unused
  1054	         compressedin,  # unused
  1055	         multicastin,  # unused
  1056	         # out
  1057	         bytes_sent,
  1058	         packets_sent,
  1059	         errout,
  1060	         dropout,
  1061	         fifoout,  # unused
  1062	         collisionsout,  # unused
  1063	         carrierout,  # unused
  1064	         compressedout) = map(int, fields)
  1065	
  1066	        retdict[name] = (bytes_sent, bytes_recv, packets_sent, packets_recv,
  1067	                         errin, errout, dropin, dropout)
  1068	    return retdict
  1069	
  1070	
  1071	def net_if_stats():
  1072	    """Get NIC stats (isup, duplex, speed, mtu)."""
  1073	    duplex_map = {cext.DUPLEX_FULL: NIC_DUPLEX_FULL,
  1074	                  cext.DUPLEX_HALF: NIC_DUPLEX_HALF,
  1075	                  cext.DUPLEX_UNKNOWN: NIC_DUPLEX_UNKNOWN}
  1076	    names = net_io_counters().keys()
  1077	    ret = {}
  1078	    for name in names:
  1079	        try:
  1080	            mtu = cext_posix.net_if_mtu(name)
  1081	            isup = cext_posix.net_if_is_running(name)
  1082	            duplex, speed = cext.net_if_duplex_speed(name)
  1083	        except OSError as err:
  1084	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1279
  1085	            if err.errno != errno.ENODEV:
  1086	                raise
  1087	            else:
  1088	                debug(err)
  1089	        else:
  1090	            ret[name] = _common.snicstats(isup, duplex_map[duplex], speed, mtu)
  1091	    return ret
  1092	
  1093	
  1094	# =====================================================================
  1095	# --- disks
  1096	# =====================================================================
  1097	
  1098	
  1099	disk_usage = _psposix.disk_usage
  1100	
  1101	
  1102	def disk_io_counters(perdisk=False):
  1103	    """Return disk I/O statistics for every disk installed on the
  1104	    system as a dict of raw tuples.
  1105	    """
  1106	    def read_procfs():
  1107	        # OK, this is a bit confusing. The format of /proc/diskstats can
  1108	        # have 3 variations.
  1109	        # On Linux 2.4 each line has always 15 fields, e.g.:
  1110	        # "3     0   8 hda 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8"
  1111	        # On Linux 2.6+ each line *usually* has 14 fields, and the disk
  1112	        # name is in another position, like this:
  1113	        # "3    0   hda 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8"
  1114	        # ...unless (Linux 2.6) the line refers to a partition instead
  1115	        # of a disk, in which case the line has less fields (7):
  1116	        # "3    1   hda1 8 8 8 8"
  1117	        # 4.18+ has 4 fields added:
  1118	        # "3    0   hda 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 0 0 0 0"
  1119	        # 5.5 has 2 more fields.
  1120	        # See:
  1121	        # https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/iostats.txt
  1122	        # https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/ABI/testing/procfs-diskstats
  1123	        with open_text("%s/diskstats" % get_procfs_path()) as f:
  1124	            lines = f.readlines()
  1125	        for line in lines:
  1126	            fields = line.split()
  1127	            flen = len(fields)
  1128	            if flen == 15:
  1129	                # Linux 2.4
  1130	                name = fields[3]
  1131	                reads = int(fields[2])
  1132	                (reads_merged, rbytes, rtime, writes, writes_merged,
  1133	                    wbytes, wtime, _, busy_time, _) = map(int, fields[4:14])
  1134	            elif flen == 14 or flen >= 18:
  1135	                # Linux 2.6+, line referring to a disk
  1136	                name = fields[2]
  1137	                (reads, reads_merged, rbytes, rtime, writes, writes_merged,
  1138	                    wbytes, wtime, _, busy_time, _) = map(int, fields[3:14])
  1139	            elif flen == 7:
  1140	                # Linux 2.6+, line referring to a partition
  1141	                name = fields[2]
  1142	                reads, rbytes, writes, wbytes = map(int, fields[3:])
  1143	                rtime = wtime = reads_merged = writes_merged = busy_time = 0
  1144	            else:
  1145	                raise ValueError("not sure how to interpret line %r" % line)
  1146	            yield (name, reads, writes, rbytes, wbytes, rtime, wtime,
  1147	                   reads_merged, writes_merged, busy_time)
  1148	
  1149	    def read_sysfs():
  1150	        for block in os.listdir('/sys/block'):
  1151	            for root, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join('/sys/block', block)):
  1152	                if 'stat' not in files:
  1153	                    continue
  1154	                with open_text(os.path.join(root, 'stat')) as f:
  1155	                    fields = f.read().strip().split()
  1156	                name = os.path.basename(root)
  1157	                (reads, reads_merged, rbytes, rtime, writes, writes_merged,
  1158	                    wbytes, wtime, _, busy_time) = map(int, fields[:10])
  1159	                yield (name, reads, writes, rbytes, wbytes, rtime,
  1160	                       wtime, reads_merged, writes_merged, busy_time)
  1161	
  1162	    if os.path.exists('%s/diskstats' % get_procfs_path()):
  1163	        gen = read_procfs()
  1164	    elif os.path.exists('/sys/block'):
  1165	        gen = read_sysfs()
  1166	    else:
  1167	        raise NotImplementedError(
  1168	            "%s/diskstats nor /sys/block filesystem are available on this "
  1169	            "system" % get_procfs_path())
  1170	
  1171	    retdict = {}
  1172	    for entry in gen:
  1173	        (name, reads, writes, rbytes, wbytes, rtime, wtime, reads_merged,
  1174	            writes_merged, busy_time) = entry
  1175	        if not perdisk and not is_storage_device(name):
  1176	            # perdisk=False means we want to calculate totals so we skip
  1177	            # partitions (e.g. 'sda1', 'nvme0n1p1') and only include
  1178	            # base disk devices (e.g. 'sda', 'nvme0n1'). Base disks
  1179	            # include a total of all their partitions + some extra size
  1180	            # of their own:
  1181	            #     $ cat /proc/diskstats
  1182	            #     259       0 sda 10485760 ...
  1183	            #     259       1 sda1 5186039 ...
  1184	            #     259       1 sda2 5082039 ...
  1185	            # See:
  1186	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/pull/1313
  1187	            continue
  1188	
  1189	        rbytes *= DISK_SECTOR_SIZE
  1190	        wbytes *= DISK_SECTOR_SIZE
  1191	        retdict[name] = (reads, writes, rbytes, wbytes, rtime, wtime,
  1192	                         reads_merged, writes_merged, busy_time)
  1193	
  1194	    return retdict
  1195	
  1196	
  1197	class RootFsDeviceFinder:
  1198	    """disk_partitions() may return partitions with device == "/dev/root"
  1199	    or "rootfs". This container class uses different strategies to try to
  1200	    obtain the real device path. Resources:
  1201	    https://bootlin.com/blog/find-root-device/
  1202	    https://www.systutorials.com/how-to-find-the-disk-where-root-is-on-in-bash-on-linux/
  1203	    """
  1204	    __slots__ = ['major', 'minor']
  1205	
  1206	    def __init__(self):
  1207	        dev = os.stat("/").st_dev
  1208	        self.major = os.major(dev)
  1209	        self.minor = os.minor(dev)
  1210	
  1211	    def ask_proc_partitions(self):
  1212	        with open_text("%s/partitions" % get_procfs_path()) as f:
  1213	            for line in f.readlines()[2:]:
  1214	                fields = line.split()
  1215	                if len(fields) < 4:  # just for extra safety
  1216	                    continue
  1217	                major = int(fields[0]) if fields[0].isdigit() else None
  1218	                minor = int(fields[1]) if fields[1].isdigit() else None
  1219	                name = fields[3]
  1220	                if major == self.major and minor == self.minor:
  1221	                    if name:  # just for extra safety
  1222	                        return "/dev/%s" % name
  1223	
  1224	    def ask_sys_dev_block(self):
  1225	        path = "/sys/dev/block/%s:%s/uevent" % (self.major, self.minor)
  1226	        with open_text(path) as f:
  1227	            for line in f:
  1228	                if line.startswith("DEVNAME="):
  1229	                    name = line.strip().rpartition("DEVNAME=")[2]
  1230	                    if name:  # just for extra safety
  1231	                        return "/dev/%s" % name
  1232	
  1233	    def ask_sys_class_block(self):
  1234	        needle = "%s:%s" % (self.major, self.minor)
  1235	        files = glob.iglob("/sys/class/block/*/dev")
  1236	        for file in files:
  1237	            try:
  1238	                f = open_text(file)
  1239	            except FileNotFoundError:  # race condition
  1240	                continue
  1241	            else:
  1242	                with f:
  1243	                    data = f.read().strip()
  1244	                    if data == needle:
  1245	                        name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(file))
  1246	                        return "/dev/%s" % name
  1247	
  1248	    def find(self):
  1249	        path = None
  1250	        if path is None:
  1251	            try:
  1252	                path = self.ask_proc_partitions()
  1253	            except (IOError, OSError) as err:
  1254	                debug(err)
  1255	        if path is None:
  1256	            try:
  1257	                path = self.ask_sys_dev_block()
  1258	            except (IOError, OSError) as err:
  1259	                debug(err)
  1260	        if path is None:
  1261	            try:
  1262	                path = self.ask_sys_class_block()
  1263	            except (IOError, OSError) as err:
  1264	                debug(err)
  1265	        # We use exists() because the "/dev/*" part of the path is hard
  1266	        # coded, so we want to be sure.
  1267	        if path is not None and os.path.exists(path):
  1268	            return path
  1269	
  1270	
  1271	def disk_partitions(all=False):
  1272	    """Return mounted disk partitions as a list of namedtuples."""
  1273	    fstypes = set()
  1274	    procfs_path = get_procfs_path()
  1275	    with open_text("%s/filesystems" % procfs_path) as f:
  1276	        for line in f:
  1277	            line = line.strip()
  1278	            if not line.startswith("nodev"):
  1279	                fstypes.add(line.strip())
  1280	            else:
  1281	                # ignore all lines starting with "nodev" except "nodev zfs"
  1282	                fstype = line.split("\t")[1]
  1283	                if fstype == "zfs":
  1284	                    fstypes.add("zfs")
  1285	
  1286	    # See: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1307
  1287	    if procfs_path == "/proc" and os.path.isfile('/etc/mtab'):
  1288	        mounts_path = os.path.realpath("/etc/mtab")
  1289	    else:
  1290	        mounts_path = os.path.realpath("%s/self/mounts" % procfs_path)
  1291	
  1292	    retlist = []
  1293	    partitions = cext.disk_partitions(mounts_path)
  1294	    for partition in partitions:
  1295	        device, mountpoint, fstype, opts = partition
  1296	        if device == 'none':
  1297	            device = ''
  1298	        if device in ("/dev/root", "rootfs"):
  1299	            device = RootFsDeviceFinder().find() or device
  1300	        if not all:
  1301	            if device == '' or fstype not in fstypes:
  1302	                continue
  1303	        maxfile = maxpath = None  # set later
  1304	        ntuple = _common.sdiskpart(device, mountpoint, fstype, opts,
  1305	                                   maxfile, maxpath)
  1306	        retlist.append(ntuple)
  1307	
  1308	    return retlist
  1309	
  1310	
  1311	# =====================================================================
  1312	# --- sensors
  1313	# =====================================================================
  1314	
  1315	
  1316	def sensors_temperatures():
  1317	    """Return hardware (CPU and others) temperatures as a dict
  1318	    including hardware name, label, current, max and critical
  1319	    temperatures.
  1320	
  1321	    Implementation notes:
  1322	    - /sys/class/hwmon looks like the most recent interface to
  1323	      retrieve this info, and this implementation relies on it
  1324	      only (old distros will probably use something else)
  1325	    - lm-sensors on Ubuntu 16.04 relies on /sys/class/hwmon
  1326	    - /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone* is another one but it's more
  1327	      difficult to parse
  1328	    """
  1329	    ret = collections.defaultdict(list)
  1330	    basenames = glob.glob('/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/temp*_*')
  1331	    # CentOS has an intermediate /device directory:
  1332	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/971
  1333	    # https://github.com/nicolargo/glances/issues/1060
  1334	    basenames.extend(glob.glob('/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/device/temp*_*'))
  1335	    basenames = sorted(set([x.split('_')[0] for x in basenames]))
  1336	
  1337	    # Only add the coretemp hwmon entries if they're not already in
  1338	    # /sys/class/hwmon/
  1339	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1708
  1340	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/pull/1648
  1341	    basenames2 = glob.glob(
  1342	        '/sys/devices/platform/coretemp.*/hwmon/hwmon*/temp*_*')
  1343	    repl = re.compile('/sys/devices/platform/coretemp.*/hwmon/')
  1344	    for name in basenames2:
  1345	        altname = repl.sub('/sys/class/hwmon/', name)
  1346	        if altname not in basenames:
  1347	            basenames.append(name)
  1348	
  1349	    for base in basenames:
  1350	        try:
  1351	            path = base + '_input'
  1352	            current = float(cat(path)) / 1000.0
  1353	            path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(base), 'name')
  1354	            unit_name = cat(path, binary=False)
  1355	        except (IOError, OSError, ValueError):
  1356	            # A lot of things can go wrong here, so let's just skip the
  1357	            # whole entry. Sure thing is Linux's /sys/class/hwmon really
  1358	            # is a stinky broken mess.
  1359	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1009
  1360	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1101
  1361	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1129
  1362	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1245
  1363	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1323
  1364	            continue
  1365	
  1366	        high = cat(base + '_max', fallback=None)
  1367	        critical = cat(base + '_crit', fallback=None)
  1368	        label = cat(base + '_label', fallback='', binary=False)
  1369	
  1370	        if high is not None:
  1371	            try:
  1372	                high = float(high) / 1000.0
  1373	            except ValueError:
  1374	                high = None
  1375	        if critical is not None:
  1376	            try:
  1377	                critical = float(critical) / 1000.0
  1378	            except ValueError:
  1379	                critical = None
  1380	
  1381	        ret[unit_name].append((label, current, high, critical))
  1382	
  1383	    # Indication that no sensors were detected in /sys/class/hwmon/
  1384	    if not basenames:
  1385	        basenames = glob.glob('/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*')
  1386	        basenames = sorted(set(basenames))
  1387	
  1388	        for base in basenames:
  1389	            try:
  1390	                path = os.path.join(base, 'temp')
  1391	                current = float(cat(path)) / 1000.0
  1392	                path = os.path.join(base, 'type')
  1393	                unit_name = cat(path, binary=False)
  1394	            except (IOError, OSError, ValueError) as err:
  1395	                debug(err)
  1396	                continue
  1397	
  1398	            trip_paths = glob.glob(base + '/trip_point*')
  1399	            trip_points = set(['_'.join(
  1400	                os.path.basename(p).split('_')[0:3]) for p in trip_paths])
  1401	            critical = None
  1402	            high = None
  1403	            for trip_point in trip_points:
  1404	                path = os.path.join(base, trip_point + "_type")
  1405	                trip_type = cat(path, fallback='', binary=False)
  1406	                if trip_type == 'critical':
  1407	                    critical = cat(os.path.join(base, trip_point + "_temp"),
  1408	                                   fallback=None)
  1409	                elif trip_type == 'high':
  1410	                    high = cat(os.path.join(base, trip_point + "_temp"),
  1411	                               fallback=None)
  1412	
  1413	                if high is not None:
  1414	                    try:
  1415	                        high = float(high) / 1000.0
  1416	                    except ValueError:
  1417	                        high = None
  1418	                if critical is not None:
  1419	                    try:
  1420	                        critical = float(critical) / 1000.0
  1421	                    except ValueError:
  1422	                        critical = None
  1423	
  1424	            ret[unit_name].append(('', current, high, critical))
  1425	
  1426	    return dict(ret)
  1427	
  1428	
  1429	def sensors_fans():
  1430	    """Return hardware fans info (for CPU and other peripherals) as a
  1431	    dict including hardware label and current speed.
  1432	
  1433	    Implementation notes:
  1434	    - /sys/class/hwmon looks like the most recent interface to
  1435	      retrieve this info, and this implementation relies on it
  1436	      only (old distros will probably use something else)
  1437	    - lm-sensors on Ubuntu 16.04 relies on /sys/class/hwmon
  1438	    """
  1439	    ret = collections.defaultdict(list)
  1440	    basenames = glob.glob('/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/fan*_*')
  1441	    if not basenames:
  1442	        # CentOS has an intermediate /device directory:
  1443	        # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/971
  1444	        basenames = glob.glob('/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/device/fan*_*')
  1445	
  1446	    basenames = sorted(set([x.split('_')[0] for x in basenames]))
  1447	    for base in basenames:
  1448	        try:
  1449	            current = int(cat(base + '_input'))
  1450	        except (IOError, OSError) as err:
  1451	            debug(err)
  1452	            continue
  1453	        unit_name = cat(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(base), 'name'),
  1454	                        binary=False)
  1455	        label = cat(base + '_label', fallback='', binary=False)
  1456	        ret[unit_name].append(_common.sfan(label, current))
  1457	
  1458	    return dict(ret)
  1459	
  1460	
  1461	def sensors_battery():
  1462	    """Return battery information.
  1463	    Implementation note: it appears /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/
  1464	    directory structure may vary and provide files with the same
  1465	    meaning but under different names, see:
  1466	    https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/966
  1467	    """
  1468	    null = object()
  1469	
  1470	    def multi_cat(*paths):
  1471	        """Attempt to read the content of multiple files which may
  1472	        not exist. If none of them exist return None.
  1473	        """
  1474	        for path in paths:
  1475	            ret = cat(path, fallback=null)
  1476	            if ret != null:
  1477	                try:
  1478	                    return int(ret)
  1479	                except ValueError:
  1480	                    return ret
  1481	        return None
  1482	
  1483	    bats = [x for x in os.listdir(POWER_SUPPLY_PATH) if x.startswith('BAT') or
  1484	            'battery' in x.lower()]
  1485	    if not bats:
  1486	        return None
  1487	    # Get the first available battery. Usually this is "BAT0", except
  1488	    # some rare exceptions:
  1489	    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1238
  1490	    root = os.path.join(POWER_SUPPLY_PATH, sorted(bats)[0])
  1491	
  1492	    # Base metrics.
  1493	    energy_now = multi_cat(
  1494	        root + "/energy_now",
  1495	        root + "/charge_now")
  1496	    power_now = multi_cat(
  1497	        root + "/power_now",
  1498	        root + "/current_now")
  1499	    energy_full = multi_cat(
  1500	        root + "/energy_full",
  1501	        root + "/charge_full")
  1502	    time_to_empty = multi_cat(root + "/time_to_empty_now")
  1503	
  1504	    # Percent. If we have energy_full the percentage will be more
  1505	    # accurate compared to reading /capacity file (float vs. int).
  1506	    if energy_full is not None and energy_now is not None:
  1507	        try:
  1508	            percent = 100.0 * energy_now / energy_full
  1509	        except ZeroDivisionError:
  1510	            percent = 0.0
  1511	    else:
  1512	        percent = int(cat(root + "/capacity", fallback=-1))
  1513	        if percent == -1:
  1514	            return None
  1515	
  1516	    # Is AC power cable plugged in?
  1517	    # Note: AC0 is not always available and sometimes (e.g. CentOS7)
  1518	    # it's called "AC".
  1519	    power_plugged = None
  1520	    online = multi_cat(
  1521	        os.path.join(POWER_SUPPLY_PATH, "AC0/online"),
  1522	        os.path.join(POWER_SUPPLY_PATH, "AC/online"))
  1523	    if online is not None:
  1524	        power_plugged = online == 1
  1525	    else:
  1526	        status = cat(root + "/status", fallback="", binary=False).lower()
  1527	        if status == "discharging":
  1528	            power_plugged = False
  1529	        elif status in ("charging", "full"):
  1530	            power_plugged = True
  1531	
  1532	    # Seconds left.
  1533	    # Note to self: we may also calculate the charging ETA as per:
  1534	    # https://github.com/thialfihar/dotfiles/blob/
  1535	    #     013937745fd9050c30146290e8f963d65c0179e6/bin/battery.py#L55
  1536	    if power_plugged:
  1537	        secsleft = _common.POWER_TIME_UNLIMITED
  1538	    elif energy_now is not None and power_now is not None:
  1539	        try:
  1540	            secsleft = int(energy_now / power_now * 3600)
  1541	        except ZeroDivisionError:
  1542	            secsleft = _common.POWER_TIME_UNKNOWN
  1543	    elif time_to_empty is not None:
  1544	        secsleft = int(time_to_empty * 60)
  1545	        if secsleft < 0:
  1546	            secsleft = _common.POWER_TIME_UNKNOWN
  1547	    else:
  1548	        secsleft = _common.POWER_TIME_UNKNOWN
  1549	
  1550	    return _common.sbattery(percent, secsleft, power_plugged)
  1551	
  1552	
  1553	# =====================================================================
  1554	# --- other system functions
  1555	# =====================================================================
  1556	
  1557	
  1558	def users():
  1559	    """Return currently connected users as a list of namedtuples."""
  1560	    retlist = []
  1561	    rawlist = cext.users()
  1562	    for item in rawlist:
  1563	        user, tty, hostname, tstamp, user_process, pid = item
  1564	        # note: the underlying C function includes entries about
  1565	        # system boot, run level and others.  We might want
  1566	        # to use them in the future.
  1567	        if not user_process:
  1568	            continue
  1569	        if hostname in (':0.0', ':0'):
  1570	            hostname = 'localhost'
  1571	        nt = _common.suser(user, tty or None, hostname, tstamp, pid)
  1572	        retlist.append(nt)
  1573	    return retlist
  1574	
  1575	
  1576	def boot_time():
  1577	    """Return the system boot time expressed in seconds since the epoch."""
  1578	    global BOOT_TIME
  1579	    path = '%s/stat' % get_procfs_path()
  1580	    with open_binary(path) as f:
  1581	        for line in f:
  1582	            if line.startswith(b'btime'):
  1583	                ret = float(line.strip().split()[1])
  1584	                BOOT_TIME = ret
  1585	                return ret
  1586	        raise RuntimeError(
  1587	            "line 'btime' not found in %s" % path)
  1588	
  1589	
  1590	# =====================================================================
  1591	# --- processes
  1592	# =====================================================================
  1593	
  1594	
  1595	def pids():
  1596	    """Returns a list of PIDs currently running on the system."""
  1597	    return [int(x) for x in os.listdir(b(get_procfs_path())) if x.isdigit()]
  1598	
  1599	
  1600	def pid_exists(pid):
  1601	    """Check for the existence of a unix PID. Linux TIDs are not
  1602	    supported (always return False).
  1603	    """
  1604	    if not _psposix.pid_exists(pid):
  1605	        return False
  1606	    else:
  1607	        # Linux's apparently does not distinguish between PIDs and TIDs
  1608	        # (thread IDs).
  1609	        # listdir("/proc") won't show any TID (only PIDs) but
  1610	        # os.stat("/proc/{tid}") will succeed if {tid} exists.
  1611	        # os.kill() can also be passed a TID. This is quite confusing.
  1612	        # In here we want to enforce this distinction and support PIDs
  1613	        # only, see:
  1614	        # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/687
  1615	        try:
  1616	            # Note: already checked that this is faster than using a
  1617	            # regular expr. Also (a lot) faster than doing
  1618	            # 'return pid in pids()'
  1619	            path = "%s/%s/status" % (get_procfs_path(), pid)
  1620	            with open_binary(path) as f:
  1621	                for line in f:
  1622	                    if line.startswith(b"Tgid:"):
  1623	                        tgid = int(line.split()[1])
  1624	                        # If tgid and pid are the same then we're
  1625	                        # dealing with a process PID.
  1626	                        return tgid == pid
  1627	                raise ValueError("'Tgid' line not found in %s" % path)
  1628	        except (EnvironmentError, ValueError):
  1629	            return pid in pids()
  1630	
  1631	
  1632	def ppid_map():
  1633	    """Obtain a {pid: ppid, ...} dict for all running processes in
  1634	    one shot. Used to speed up Process.children().
  1635	    """
  1636	    ret = {}
  1637	    procfs_path = get_procfs_path()
  1638	    for pid in pids():
  1639	        try:
  1640	            with open_binary("%s/%s/stat" % (procfs_path, pid)) as f:
  1641	                data = f.read()
  1642	        except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
  1643	            # Note: we should be able to access /stat for all processes
  1644	            # aka it's unlikely we'll bump into EPERM, which is good.
  1645	            pass
  1646	        else:
  1647	            rpar = data.rfind(b')')
  1648	            dset = data[rpar + 2:].split()
  1649	            ppid = int(dset[1])
  1650	            ret[pid] = ppid
  1651	    return ret
  1652	
  1653	
  1654	def wrap_exceptions(fun):
  1655	    """Decorator which translates bare OSError and IOError exceptions
  1656	    into NoSuchProcess and AccessDenied.
  1657	    """
  1658	    @functools.wraps(fun)
  1659	    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):
  1660	        try:
  1661	            return fun(self, *args, **kwargs)
  1662	        except PermissionError:
  1663	            raise AccessDenied(self.pid, self._name)
  1664	        except ProcessLookupError:
  1665	            raise NoSuchProcess(self.pid, self._name)
  1666	        except FileNotFoundError:
  1667	            if not os.path.exists("%s/%s" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)):
  1668	                raise NoSuchProcess(self.pid, self._name)
  1669	            # Note: zombies will keep existing under /proc until they're
  1670	            # gone so there's no way to distinguish them in here.
  1671	            raise
  1672	    return wrapper
  1673	
  1674	
  1675	class Process(object):
  1676	    """Linux process implementation."""
  1677	
  1678	    __slots__ = ["pid", "_name", "_ppid", "_procfs_path", "_cache"]
  1679	
  1680	    def __init__(self, pid):
  1681	        self.pid = pid
  1682	        self._name = None
  1683	        self._ppid = None
  1684	        self._procfs_path = get_procfs_path()
  1685	
  1686	    def _assert_alive(self):
  1687	        """Raise NSP if the process disappeared on us."""
  1688	        # For those C function who do not raise NSP, possibly returning
  1689	        # incorrect or incomplete result.
  1690	        os.stat('%s/%s' % (self._procfs_path, self.pid))
  1691	
  1692	    @wrap_exceptions
  1693	    @memoize_when_activated
  1694	    def _parse_stat_file(self):
  1695	        """Parse /proc/{pid}/stat file and return a dict with various
  1696	        process info.
  1697	        Using "man proc" as a reference: where "man proc" refers to
  1698	        position N always substract 3 (e.g ppid position 4 in
  1699	        'man proc' == position 1 in here).
  1700	        The return value is cached in case oneshot() ctx manager is
  1701	        in use.
  1702	        """
  1703	        with open_binary("%s/%s/stat" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
  1704	            data = f.read()
  1705	        # Process name is between parentheses. It can contain spaces and
  1706	        # other parentheses. This is taken into account by looking for
  1707	        # the first occurrence of "(" and the last occurence of ")".
  1708	        rpar = data.rfind(b')')
  1709	        name = data[data.find(b'(') + 1:rpar]
  1710	        fields = data[rpar + 2:].split()
  1711	
  1712	        ret = {}
  1713	        ret['name'] = name
  1714	        ret['status'] = fields[0]
  1715	        ret['ppid'] = fields[1]
  1716	        ret['ttynr'] = fields[4]
  1717	        ret['utime'] = fields[11]
  1718	        ret['stime'] = fields[12]
  1719	        ret['children_utime'] = fields[13]
  1720	        ret['children_stime'] = fields[14]
  1721	        ret['create_time'] = fields[19]
  1722	        ret['cpu_num'] = fields[36]
  1723	        ret['blkio_ticks'] = fields[39]  # aka 'delayacct_blkio_ticks'
  1724	
  1725	        return ret
  1726	
  1727	    @wrap_exceptions
  1728	    @memoize_when_activated
  1729	    def _read_status_file(self):
  1730	        """Read /proc/{pid}/stat file and return its content.
  1731	        The return value is cached in case oneshot() ctx manager is
  1732	        in use.
  1733	        """
  1734	        with open_binary("%s/%s/status" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
  1735	            return f.read()
  1736	
  1737	    @wrap_exceptions
  1738	    @memoize_when_activated
  1739	    def _read_smaps_file(self):
  1740	        with open_binary("%s/%s/smaps" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid),
  1741	                         buffering=BIGFILE_BUFFERING) as f:
  1742	            return f.read().strip()
  1743	
  1744	    def oneshot_enter(self):
  1745	        self._parse_stat_file.cache_activate(self)
  1746	        self._read_status_file.cache_activate(self)
  1747	        self._read_smaps_file.cache_activate(self)
  1748	
  1749	    def oneshot_exit(self):
  1750	        self._parse_stat_file.cache_deactivate(self)
  1751	        self._read_status_file.cache_deactivate(self)
  1752	        self._read_smaps_file.cache_deactivate(self)
  1753	
  1754	    @wrap_exceptions
  1755	    def name(self):
  1756	        name = self._parse_stat_file()['name']
  1757	        if PY3:
  1758	            name = decode(name)
  1759	        # XXX - gets changed later and probably needs refactoring
  1760	        return name
  1761	
  1762	    def exe(self):
  1763	        try:
  1764	            return readlink("%s/%s/exe" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid))
  1765	        except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
  1766	            # no such file error; might be raised also if the
  1767	            # path actually exists for system processes with
  1768	            # low pids (about 0-20)
  1769	            if os.path.lexists("%s/%s" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)):
  1770	                return ""
  1771	            else:
  1772	                if not pid_exists(self.pid):
  1773	                    raise NoSuchProcess(self.pid, self._name)
  1774	                else:
  1775	                    raise ZombieProcess(self.pid, self._name, self._ppid)
  1776	        except PermissionError:
  1777	            raise AccessDenied(self.pid, self._name)
  1778	
  1779	    @wrap_exceptions
  1780	    def cmdline(self):
  1781	        with open_text("%s/%s/cmdline" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
  1782	            data = f.read()
  1783	        if not data:
  1784	            # may happen in case of zombie process
  1785	            return []
  1786	        # 'man proc' states that args are separated by null bytes '\0'
  1787	        # and last char is supposed to be a null byte. Nevertheless
  1788	        # some processes may change their cmdline after being started
  1789	        # (via setproctitle() or similar), they are usually not
  1790	        # compliant with this rule and use spaces instead. Google
  1791	        # Chrome process is an example. See:
  1792	        # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1179
  1793	        sep = '\x00' if data.endswith('\x00') else ' '
  1794	        if data.endswith(sep):
  1795	            data = data[:-1]
  1796	        cmdline = data.split(sep)
  1797	        # Sometimes last char is a null byte '\0' but the args are
  1798	        # separated by spaces, see: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/
  1799	        # issues/1179#issuecomment-552984549
  1800	        if sep == '\x00' and len(cmdline) == 1 and ' ' in data:
  1801	            cmdline = data.split(' ')
  1802	        return cmdline
  1803	
  1804	    @wrap_exceptions
  1805	    def environ(self):
  1806	        with open_text("%s/%s/environ" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
  1807	            data = f.read()
  1808	        return parse_environ_block(data)
  1809	
  1810	    @wrap_exceptions
  1811	    def terminal(self):
  1812	        tty_nr = int(self._parse_stat_file()['ttynr'])
  1813	        tmap = _psposix.get_terminal_map()
  1814	        try:
  1815	            return tmap[tty_nr]
  1816	        except KeyError:
  1817	            return None
  1818	
  1819	    # May not be available on old kernels.
  1820	    if os.path.exists('/proc/%s/io' % os.getpid()):
  1821	        @wrap_exceptions
  1822	        def io_counters(self):
  1823	            fname = "%s/%s/io" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)
  1824	            fields = {}
  1825	            with open_binary(fname) as f:
  1826	                for line in f:
  1827	                    # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1004
  1828	                    line = line.strip()
  1829	                    if line:
  1830	                        try:
  1831	                            name, value = line.split(b': ')
  1832	                        except ValueError:
  1833	                            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/1004
  1834	                            continue
  1835	                        else:
  1836	                            fields[name] = int(value)
  1837	            if not fields:
  1838	                raise RuntimeError("%s file was empty" % fname)
  1839	            try:
  1840	                return pio(
  1841	                    fields[b'syscr'],  # read syscalls
  1842	                    fields[b'syscw'],  # write syscalls
  1843	                    fields[b'read_bytes'],  # read bytes
  1844	                    fields[b'write_bytes'],  # write bytes
  1845	                    fields[b'rchar'],  # read chars
  1846	                    fields[b'wchar'],  # write chars
  1847	                )
  1848	            except KeyError as err:
  1849	                raise ValueError("%r field was not found in %s; found fields "
  1850	                                 "are %r" % (err[0], fname, fields))
  1851	
  1852	    @wrap_exceptions
  1853	    def cpu_times(self):
  1854	        values = self._parse_stat_file()
  1855	        utime = float(values['utime']) / CLOCK_TICKS
  1856	        stime = float(values['stime']) / CLOCK_TICKS
  1857	        children_utime = float(values['children_utime']) / CLOCK_TICKS
  1858	        children_stime = float(values['children_stime']) / CLOCK_TICKS
  1859	        iowait = float(values['blkio_ticks']) / CLOCK_TICKS
  1860	        return pcputimes(utime, stime, children_utime, children_stime, iowait)
  1861	
  1862	    @wrap_exceptions
  1863	    def cpu_num(self):
  1864	        """What CPU the process is on."""
  1865	        return int(self._parse_stat_file()['cpu_num'])
  1866	
  1867	    @wrap_exceptions
  1868	    def wait(self, timeout=None):
  1869	        return _psposix.wait_pid(self.pid, timeout, self._name)
  1870	
  1871	    @wrap_exceptions
  1872	    def create_time(self):
  1873	        ctime = float(self._parse_stat_file()['create_time'])
  1874	        # According to documentation, starttime is in field 21 and the
  1875	        # unit is jiffies (clock ticks).
  1876	        # We first divide it for clock ticks and then add uptime returning
  1877	        # seconds since the epoch.
  1878	        # Also use cached value if available.
  1879	        bt = BOOT_TIME or boot_time()
  1880	        return (ctime / CLOCK_TICKS) + bt
  1881	
  1882	    @wrap_exceptions
  1883	    def memory_info(self):
  1884	        #  ============================================================
  1885	        # | FIELD  | DESCRIPTION                         | AKA  | TOP  |
  1886	        #  ============================================================
  1887	        # | rss    | resident set size                   |      | RES  |
  1888	        # | vms    | total program size                  | size | VIRT |
  1889	        # | shared | shared pages (from shared mappings) |      | SHR  |
  1890	        # | text   | text ('code')                       | trs  | CODE |
  1891	        # | lib    | library (unused in Linux 2.6)       | lrs  |      |
  1892	        # | data   | data + stack                        | drs  | DATA |
  1893	        # | dirty  | dirty pages (unused in Linux 2.6)   | dt   |      |
  1894	        #  ============================================================
  1895	        with open_binary("%s/%s/statm" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
  1896	            vms, rss, shared, text, lib, data, dirty = \
  1897	                [int(x) * PAGESIZE for x in f.readline().split()[:7]]
  1898	        return pmem(rss, vms, shared, text, lib, data, dirty)
  1899	
  1900	    # /proc/pid/smaps does not exist on kernels < 2.6.14 or if
  1901	    # CONFIG_MMU kernel configuration option is not enabled.
  1902	    if HAS_SMAPS:
  1903	
  1904	        @wrap_exceptions
  1905	        def memory_full_info(
  1906	                self,
  1907	                # Gets Private_Clean, Private_Dirty, Private_Hugetlb.
  1908	                _private_re=re.compile(br"\nPrivate.*:\s+(\d+)"),
  1909	                _pss_re=re.compile(br"\nPss\:\s+(\d+)"),
  1910	                _swap_re=re.compile(br"\nSwap\:\s+(\d+)")):
  1911	            basic_mem = self.memory_info()
  1912	            # Note: using 3 regexes is faster than reading the file
  1913	            # line by line.
  1914	            # XXX: on Python 3 the 2 regexes are 30% slower than on
  1915	            # Python 2 though. Figure out why.
  1916	            #
  1917	            # You might be tempted to calculate USS by subtracting
  1918	            # the "shared" value from the "resident" value in
  1919	            # /proc/<pid>/statm. But at least on Linux, statm's "shared"
  1920	            # value actually counts pages backed by files, which has
  1921	            # little to do with whether the pages are actually shared.
  1922	            # /proc/self/smaps on the other hand appears to give us the
  1923	            # correct information.
  1924	            smaps_data = self._read_smaps_file()
  1925	            # Note: smaps file can be empty for certain processes.
  1926	            # The code below will not crash though and will result to 0.
  1927	            uss = sum(map(int, _private_re.findall(smaps_data))) * 1024
  1928	            pss = sum(map(int, _pss_re.findall(smaps_data))) * 1024
  1929	            swap = sum(map(int, _swap_re.findall(smaps_data))) * 1024
  1930	            return pfullmem(*basic_mem + (uss, pss, swap))
  1931	
  1932	    else:
  1933	        memory_full_info = memory_info
  1934	
  1935	    if HAS_SMAPS:
  1936	
  1937	        @wrap_exceptions
  1938	        def memory_maps(self):
  1939	            """Return process's mapped memory regions as a list of named
  1940	            tuples. Fields are explained in 'man proc'; here is an updated
  1941	            (Apr 2012) version: http://goo.gl/fmebo
  1942	
  1943	            /proc/{PID}/smaps does not exist on kernels < 2.6.14 or if
  1944	            CONFIG_MMU kernel configuration option is not enabled.
  1945	            """
  1946	            def get_blocks(lines, current_block):
  1947	                data = {}
  1948	                for line in lines:
  1949	                    fields = line.split(None, 5)
  1950	                    if not fields[0].endswith(b':'):
  1951	                        # new block section
  1952	                        yield (current_block.pop(), data)
  1953	                        current_block.append(line)
  1954	                    else:
  1955	                        try:
  1956	                            data[fields[0]] = int(fields[1]) * 1024
  1957	                        except ValueError:
  1958	                            if fields[0].startswith(b'VmFlags:'):
  1959	                                # see issue #369
  1960	                                continue
  1961	                            else:
  1962	                                raise ValueError("don't know how to inte"
  1963	                                                 "rpret line %r" % line)
  1964	                yield (current_block.pop(), data)
  1965	
  1966	            data = self._read_smaps_file()
  1967	            # Note: smaps file can be empty for certain processes.
  1968	            if not data:
  1969	                return []
  1970	            lines = data.split(b'\n')
  1971	            ls = []
  1972	            first_line = lines.pop(0)
  1973	            current_block = [first_line]
  1974	            for header, data in get_blocks(lines, current_block):
  1975	                hfields = header.split(None, 5)
  1976	                try:
  1977	                    addr, perms, offset, dev, inode, path = hfields
  1978	                except ValueError:
  1979	                    addr, perms, offset, dev, inode, path = \
  1980	                        hfields + ['']
  1981	                if not path:
  1982	                    path = '[anon]'
  1983	                else:
  1984	                    if PY3:
  1985	                        path = decode(path)
  1986	                    path = path.strip()
  1987	                    if (path.endswith(' (deleted)') and not
  1988	                            path_exists_strict(path)):
  1989	                        path = path[:-10]
  1990	                ls.append((
  1991	                    decode(addr), decode(perms), path,
  1992	                    data.get(b'Rss:', 0),
  1993	                    data.get(b'Size:', 0),
  1994	                    data.get(b'Pss:', 0),
  1995	                    data.get(b'Shared_Clean:', 0),
  1996	                    data.get(b'Shared_Dirty:', 0),
  1997	                    data.get(b'Private_Clean:', 0),
  1998	                    data.get(b'Private_Dirty:', 0),
  1999	                    data.get(b'Referenced:', 0),
  2000	                    data.get(b'Anonymous:', 0),
  2001	                    data.get(b'Swap:', 0)
  2002	                ))
  2003	            return ls
  2004	
  2005	    @wrap_exceptions
  2006	    def cwd(self):
  2007	        try:
  2008	            return readlink("%s/%s/cwd" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid))
  2009	        except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
  2010	            # https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/986
  2011	            if not pid_exists(self.pid):
  2012	                raise NoSuchProcess(self.pid, self._name)
  2013	            else:
  2014	                raise ZombieProcess(self.pid, self._name, self._ppid)
  2015	
  2016	    @wrap_exceptions
  2017	    def num_ctx_switches(self,
  2018	                         _ctxsw_re=re.compile(br'ctxt_switches:\t(\d+)')):
  2019	        data = self._read_status_file()
  2020	        ctxsw = _ctxsw_re.findall(data)
  2021	        if not ctxsw:
  2022	            raise NotImplementedError(
  2023	                "'voluntary_ctxt_switches' and 'nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches'"
  2024	                "lines were not found in %s/%s/status; the kernel is "
  2025	                "probably older than 2.6.23" % (
  2026	                    self._procfs_path, self.pid))
  2027	        else:
  2028	            return _common.pctxsw(int(ctxsw[0]), int(ctxsw[1]))
  2029	
  2030	    @wrap_exceptions
  2031	    def num_threads(self, _num_threads_re=re.compile(br'Threads:\t(\d+)')):
  2032	        # Note: on Python 3 using a re is faster than iterating over file
  2033	        # line by line. On Python 2 is the exact opposite, and iterating
  2034	        # over a file on Python 3 is slower than on Python 2.
  2035	        data = self._read_status_file()
  2036	        return int(_num_threads_re.findall(data)[0])
  2037	
  2038	    @wrap_exceptions
  2039	    def threads(self):
  2040	        thread_ids = os.listdir("%s/%s/task" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid))
  2041	        thread_ids.sort()
  2042	        retlist = []
  2043	        hit_enoent = False
  2044	        for thread_id in thread_ids:
  2045	            fname = "%s/%s/task/%s/stat" % (
  2046	                self._procfs_path, self.pid, thread_id)
  2047	            try:
  2048	                with open_binary(fname) as f:
  2049	                    st = f.read().strip()
  2050	            except FileNotFoundError:
  2051	                # no such file or directory; it means thread
  2052	                # disappeared on us
  2053	                hit_enoent = True
  2054	                continue
  2055	            # ignore the first two values ("pid (exe)")
  2056	            st = st[st.find(b')') + 2:]
  2057	            values = st.split(b' ')
  2058	            utime = float(values[11]) / CLOCK_TICKS
  2059	            stime = float(values[12]) / CLOCK_TICKS
  2060	            ntuple = _common.pthread(int(thread_id), utime, stime)
  2061	            retlist.append(ntuple)
  2062	        if hit_enoent:
  2063	            self._assert_alive()
  2064	        return retlist
  2065	
  2066	    @wrap_exceptions
  2067	    def nice_get(self):
  2068	        # with open_text('%s/%s/stat' % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
  2069	        #   data = f.read()
  2070	        #   return int(data.split()[18])
  2071	
  2072	        # Use C implementation
  2073	        return cext_posix.getpriority(self.pid)
  2074	
  2075	    @wrap_exceptions
  2076	    def nice_set(self, value):
  2077	        return cext_posix.setpriority(self.pid, value)
  2078	
  2079	    # starting from CentOS 6.
  2080	    if HAS_CPU_AFFINITY:
  2081	
  2082	        @wrap_exceptions
  2083	        def cpu_affinity_get(self):
  2084	            return cext.proc_cpu_affinity_get(self.pid)
  2085	
  2086	        def _get_eligible_cpus(
  2087	                self, _re=re.compile(br"Cpus_allowed_list:\t(\d+)-(\d+)")):
  2088	            # See: https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/issues/956
  2089	            data = self._read_status_file()
  2090	            match = _re.findall(data)
  2091	            if match:
  2092	                return list(range(int(match[0][0]), int(match[0][1]) + 1))
  2093	            else:
  2094	                return list(range(len(per_cpu_times())))
  2095	
  2096	        @wrap_exceptions
  2097	        def cpu_affinity_set(self, cpus):
  2098	            try:
  2099	                cext.proc_cpu_affinity_set(self.pid, cpus)
  2100	            except (OSError, ValueError) as err:
  2101	                if isinstance(err, ValueError) or err.errno == errno.EINVAL:
  2102	                    eligible_cpus = self._get_eligible_cpus()
  2103	                    all_cpus = tuple(range(len(per_cpu_times())))
  2104	                    for cpu in cpus:
  2105	                        if cpu not in all_cpus:
  2106	                            raise ValueError(
  2107	                                "invalid CPU number %r; choose between %s" % (
  2108	                                    cpu, eligible_cpus))
  2109	                        if cpu not in eligible_cpus:
  2110	                            raise ValueError(
  2111	                                "CPU number %r is not eligible; choose "
  2112	                                "between %s" % (cpu, eligible_cpus))
  2113	                raise
  2114	
  2115	    # only starting from kernel 2.6.13
  2116	    if HAS_PROC_IO_PRIORITY:
  2117	
  2118	        @wrap_exceptions
  2119	        def ionice_get(self):
  2120	            ioclass, value = cext.proc_ioprio_get(self.pid)
  2121	            if enum is not None:
  2122	                ioclass = IOPriority(ioclass)
  2123	            return _common.pionice(ioclass, value)
  2124	
  2125	        @wrap_exceptions
  2126	        def ionice_set(self, ioclass, value):
  2127	            if value is None:
  2128	                value = 0
  2129	            if value and ioclass in (IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE, IOPRIO_CLASS_NONE):
  2130	                raise ValueError("%r ioclass accepts no value" % ioclass)
  2131	            if value < 0 or value > 7:
  2132	                raise ValueError("value not in 0-7 range")
  2133	            return cext.proc_ioprio_set(self.pid, ioclass, value)
  2134	
  2135	    if prlimit is not None:
  2136	
  2137	        @wrap_exceptions
  2138	        def rlimit(self, resource_, limits=None):
  2139	            # If pid is 0 prlimit() applies to the calling process and
  2140	            # we don't want that. We should never get here though as
  2141	            # PID 0 is not supported on Linux.
  2142	            if self.pid == 0:
  2143	                raise ValueError("can't use prlimit() against PID 0 process")
  2144	            try:
  2145	                if limits is None:
  2146	                    # get
  2147	                    return prlimit(self.pid, resource_)
  2148	                else:
  2149	                    # set
  2150	                    if len(limits) != 2:
  2151	                        raise ValueError(
  2152	                            "second argument must be a (soft, hard) tuple, "
  2153	                            "got %s" % repr(limits))
  2154	                    prlimit(self.pid, resource_, limits)
  2155	            except OSError as err:
  2156	                if err.errno == errno.ENOSYS and pid_exists(self.pid):
  2157	                    # I saw this happening on Travis:
  2158	                    # https://travis-ci.org/giampaolo/psutil/jobs/51368273
  2159	                    raise ZombieProcess(self.pid, self._name, self._ppid)
  2160	                else:
  2161	                    raise
  2162	
  2163	    @wrap_exceptions
  2164	    def status(self):
  2165	        letter = self._parse_stat_file()['status']
  2166	        if PY3:
  2167	            letter = letter.decode()
  2168	        # XXX is '?' legit? (we're not supposed to return it anyway)
  2169	        return PROC_STATUSES.get(letter, '?')
  2170	
  2171	    @wrap_exceptions
  2172	    def open_files(self):
  2173	        retlist = []
  2174	        files = os.listdir("%s/%s/fd" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid))
  2175	        hit_enoent = False
  2176	        for fd in files:
  2177	            file = "%s/%s/fd/%s" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid, fd)
  2178	            try:
  2179	                path = readlink(file)
  2180	            except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
  2181	                # ENOENT == file which is gone in the meantime
  2182	                hit_enoent = True
  2183	                continue
  2184	            except OSError as err:
  2185	                if err.errno == errno.EINVAL:
  2186	                    # not a link
  2187	                    continue
  2188	                if err.errno == errno.ENAMETOOLONG:
  2189	                    # file name too long
  2190	                    debug(err)
  2191	                    continue
  2192	                raise
  2193	            else:
  2194	                # If path is not an absolute there's no way to tell
  2195	                # whether it's a regular file or not, so we skip it.
  2196	                # A regular file is always supposed to be have an
  2197	                # absolute path though.
  2198	                if path.startswith('/') and isfile_strict(path):
  2199	                    # Get file position and flags.
  2200	                    file = "%s/%s/fdinfo/%s" % (
  2201	                        self._procfs_path, self.pid, fd)
  2202	                    try:
  2203	                        with open_binary(file) as f:
  2204	                            pos = int(f.readline().split()[1])
  2205	                            flags = int(f.readline().split()[1], 8)
  2206	                    except FileNotFoundError:
  2207	                        # fd gone in the meantime; process may
  2208	                        # still be alive
  2209	                        hit_enoent = True
  2210	                    else:
  2211	                        mode = file_flags_to_mode(flags)
  2212	                        ntuple = popenfile(
  2213	                            path, int(fd), int(pos), mode, flags)
  2214	                        retlist.append(ntuple)
  2215	        if hit_enoent:
  2216	            self._assert_alive()
  2217	        return retlist
  2218	
  2219	    @wrap_exceptions
  2220	    def connections(self, kind='inet'):
  2221	        ret = _connections.retrieve(kind, self.pid)
  2222	        self._assert_alive()
  2223	        return ret
  2224	
  2225	    @wrap_exceptions
  2226	    def num_fds(self):
  2227	        return len(os.listdir("%s/%s/fd" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)))
  2228	
  2229	    @wrap_exceptions
  2230	    def ppid(self):
  2231	        return int(self._parse_stat_file()['ppid'])
  2232	
  2233	    @wrap_exceptions
  2234	    def uids(self, _uids_re=re.compile(br'Uid:\t(\d+)\t(\d+)\t(\d+)')):
  2235	        data = self._read_status_file()
  2236	        real, effective, saved = _uids_re.findall(data)[0]
  2237	        return _common.puids(int(real), int(effective), int(saved))
  2238	
  2239	    @wrap_exceptions
  2240	    def gids(self, _gids_re=re.compile(br'Gid:\t(\d+)\t(\d+)\t(\d+)')):
  2241	        data = self._read_status_file()
  2242	        real, effective, saved = _gids_re.findall(data)[0]
  2243	        return _common.pgids(int(real), int(effective), int(saved))
